title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This playbook is the canonical Customer Success & Support guide for enterprise onboarding, escalation procedures, integration guidance, known issues and workarounds, support process, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs who are responsible for delivering and operating Redwood Inference for enterprise customers.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments, and production-hosted customers with enterprise agreements).
- Covers pre-sales handoff through 90-day post-go-live, ongoing support levels, and QBR cadence.

Owners & Contacts:
- Document owner: Priya Shah (Customer Success)
- Oncall support: eng-sre@redwood.com (pager)
- Escalation manager: Ethan Rodriguez (Support Engineering)
- Solutions Engineering contact: Lina Gomez
- Account lead / CSM: Assigned per customer

Prerequisites before onboarding kickoff:
1. Contract & legal checklist complete (billing, data residency, confidentiality)
2. Customer has completed the security questionnaire or an SOC2/data processing addendum is signed if required.
3. Dedicated or Private deployment provisioning started (if applicable) and cloud accounts confirmed.
4. Technical contacts and stakeholder matrix provided (names, roles, emails, Slack).

Kickoff agenda (standard 60–90m):
1. Introductions & goals (owner: CSM)
2. Success criteria & KPIs (uptime, latency P95, cost/unit targets, accuracy/regression tolerances)
3. Timeline & milestones (provisioning, integration, validation, cutover)
4. Roles & RACI (see table below)
5. Communication plan (regular sync cadence, Slack channel, escalation paths)
6. Next steps & immediate action items

RACI (example):
- CSM: Customer success lead, process owner for onboarding and QBRs
- SE: Technical integration, API keys, test dataset validation
- SRE: Capacity planning, infra provisioning, runbooks for failover
- Support Engineering: Day-2 support, incident triage, escalations

Onboarding phases & checklist:
1) Pre-provision (owners: CSM, SE)
- Verify contract and account setup
- Collect network allowlists, egress rules, and IP allowlist for Dedicated/Private
- Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and key rotation policy
- Define data residency & retention settings

2) Provisioning (owners: SRE, eng-private-deployments)
- Allocate dedicated capacity or deploy private control plane
- Validate TLS certificates and domain names
- Run initial smoke tests (see smoke test commands below)

3) Integration (owners: SE)
- Deliver integration guide and sample SDK snippets
- Exchange API keys (customer-managed secrets recommended for Private)
- Implement auth and retry/backoff logic per SDK guidelines
- Configure batching and cache settings to meet cost/latency targets

4) Validation (owners: SE, QA)
- Run customer test-suite (functional + performance)
- Validate P95 latency, throughput, and model quality on sample prompts
- Complete security checklist and verify audit logging

5) Training & Handover (owners: CSM, SE)
- Conduct runbook training for customer ops & internal support
- Create a shared incident response channel and access for oncall engineers
- Handover artifact: integration checklist, test results, runbooks, contact matrix

6) Post-go-live (0–90 days) (owners: CSM, Support Engineering)
- Daily check-ins for first 14 days, weekly for next 60 days
- Collect early usage metrics, error rates, and quality feedback
- Schedule first 30/60/90 day QBRs

Smoke test commands (examples):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"input":"smoke test"}'
- python -c "import requests; print(requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer <KEY>'}, json={'input':['test']}).status_code)"

Integration guide (high-level):
- Authentication: API keys (hosted) or mTLS + API key (Private). For Private deployments, use customer KMS integration patterns from confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.
- Rate limiting: Respect per-customer rate limits configured in the Console. Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429s.
- Batching: Use SDK batching helpers; recommended batch size depends on model and latency SLO (common starting point: 8–16 requests per batch for embeddings, 4–8 for generation).
- Caching: Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts. Typical TTLs: 5–60 minutes depending on workload.
- Observability hooks: Instrument request IDs, model name/version, route, and customer_id for tracing and cost attribution.

Sample integration checklist (table-style text):
- API key obtained: Yes/No
- Endpoints whitelisted: Yes/No
- Test corpus uploaded: Yes/No
- Baseline latency measured: P50/P95
- Quality baseline (sample prompts) approved: Yes/No

Escalation playbook (executive summary):
- Severity levels (definitions & targets):
  - Sev 1 (critical): Production outage affecting all users; target initial response 15 minutes; resolution target 4 hours (mitigation within 1 hour).
  - Sev 2 (high): Significant degradation for many users or severe quality regression; response 30 minutes; resolution target 24 hours.
  - Sev 3 (medium): Functional impact for a subset of users or noncritical performance degradation; response 4 business hours; resolution target 3 business days.
  - Sev 4 (low): Minor bugs, feature requests; response 1 business day; resolution per backlog/planning.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage by L1 support: Validate customer claim, reproduce, collect logs and request-id, escalate to Support Engineering if not resolvable within 60 minutes.
2. Support Engineering (L2): Run diagnostic playbooks, consult runtime runbooks (confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks), and engage SRE if infrastructure or capacity issue suspected.
3. SRE/Platform: Execute remediation (capacity increases, failover, kernel patch) and communicate mitigation ETA.
4. Engineering/Model team: Engage for model quality regressions or kernel-level bugs; coordinate hotfix or rollback.
5. Executive notification: Triggered for Sev 1 and extended Sev 2 incidents; includes account lead, CRO, CTO as appropriate per SLA.

Contact matrix (text):
- L1 Support: support@redwood.com (monitored 24/7)
- L2 Support Engineering: se-support@redwood.com (paged on Sev 1/2)
- SRE Oncall: eng-sre@redwood.com (pager)
- Customer Success escalation: CSM oncall roster (CSM pager)

Communication templates (burndown / status updates):
- Initial acknowledgement (within SLA): short summary, severity, expected next update time.
- Mitigation update: steps taken, temporary mitigations, ETA for fix.
- Post-incident report: root cause, timeline, corrective actions, preventive measures.

Known issues & workarounds (representative):
1) Issue: Intermittent 503s for generation endpoints when autoscaler scales up new nodes.
   Symptoms: Elevated 5xx rate during scale events; P95 latency spikes.
   Workaround: Increase initial warm pool size or use circuit-breaker with short retry window; SRE can set autoscaler stabilization window to 120s as a temporary measure.

2) Issue: Embeddings mismatch after model variant rollback.
   Symptoms: Downstream search ranking shifted; semantic search results inconsistent.
   Workaround: Reindex data with the active embeddings model; pin embedding model version in application config to avoid unexpected rollbacks.

3) Issue: Private deployment cert rotation fails for older control-plane images.
   Symptoms: API connectivity errors post-cert-rotation.
   Workaround: Apply the control-plane patch v1.12.3 or re-run cert-rotation helm job with --force-legacy flag per eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback guidance.

Support process (ticket lifecycle):
1. Ticket intake (Support portal / email / Slack): automatic intake with metadata (customer_id, environment, route, request-id).
2. Triage: L1 assigns severity, reproduces, and adds requested artifacts (logs, request-ids, timeline).
3. L2 investigation: Deep diagnostics, engage product/engineering as needed.
4. Resolution & QA: Implement fix, validate with customer test corpus.
5. Closure: Document root cause and corrective actions; schedule postmortem for Sev 1 incidents.

SLA targets (for enterprise customers):
- Response times: Sev1 15m, Sev2 30m, Sev3 4h, Sev4 24h
- Resolution/execution: per severity as defined above; contractual SLA in customer contract overrides this playbook.

Routine health checks (daily/weekly):
Daily (automated + CSM check):
- API error rate (5xx) < 0.5% or baseline+X
- P95 latency within 20% of baseline
- Token consumption within expected budget (daily spike check)
- Model quality alerts: error in eval or regression alert triggered

Weekly (CSM + SE):
- Usage trend report (tokens, requests, embeddings units)
- Cost-per-token trends and batching/caching efficiency
- SLO adherence: uptime, latency, error budget burn
- Open tickets & escalations review

Health check template (fields):
- Date
- Customer
- Environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- P50/P95 latency (ms)
- Error rate (5xx)
- Throughput (req/s)
- Active sessions or connections
- Recent incidents (7d)
- Action items & owners

QBR playbook and materials:
- Cadence: First QBR at 30 days post-go-live, then quarterly. For strategic customers, monthly reviews in first quarter recommended.
- QBR attendees: CSM, Customer engineering lead, Solutions Engineer, Support lead, Account Executive (optional)
- Standard QBR agenda:
  1) Executive summary & success metrics
  2) Usage & cost trends (tokens, embeddings, model choices)
  3) Reliability & incidents (SLOs, incidents, actions taken)
  4) Model quality and experiments (A/B tests, evals)
  5) Roadmap & upcoming features impacting the customer
  6) Action items & owners

QBR deliverables (templates):
- Slide deck template: executive summary, metrics snapshots, incident summary, roadmap impact table
- Action tracker: table of open items, owners, due dates
- Follow-up email template: summary, next steps, attachments

Monitoring & dashboards (recommended):
- Per-customer Console dashboard with token usage, latency histograms, per-route cost breakdown
- Alerting rules: high error rate (>1%), sustained P95 increase (>30% over baseline), unusual token consumption bursts
- Traces: integrate request-id across frontend -> API -> runtime to correlate errors and latencies

Playbook references & artifacts:
- Runtime runbooks: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Private deployment guides: confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides
- Incident review template: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems
- Integration SDKs & examples: confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples

Appendix A — Example status update cadence for Sev1:
- 00:00: Acknowledge & initial triage (15m)
- 00:15: Initial update to customer (status, short-term mitigation)
- 01:00: Technical deep-dive update (diagnostic findings, next steps)
- Every 60 minutes thereafter until mitigation
- Post-mitigation: 24h follow-up and 72h root-cause report

Appendix B — Quick troubleshooting checklist for Support Engineers:
1. Collect request-id and full timestamp range
2. Check API gateway logs for 429/503/5xx spikes
3. Query runtime metrics for queue length, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate
4. Run smoke test against control-plane and compare latency
5. If model-quality regression suspected, pull evaluation harness results from applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness
